source: The project's own authoritative taxonomy, transcribed from source — not author-constructed.

construction.feature_modules: Each src/OrchardCore.Modules/<Module>/Manifest.cs declares a `Category = "..."` attribute (OrchardCore's own module taxonomy, surfaced in its admin UI and docs). The module .csproj is assigned verbatim to its declared Category. 91 modules across 28 categories; one module (OrchardCore.Mvc.HelloWorld, a sample) has no Category and is mapped to `Uncategorized`.
construction.framework: src/OrchardCore/* projects are the framework, not feature modules, so they carry no Category. They are split by OrchardCore's pervasive, documented `.Abstractions` convention into `Framework Abstractions` (interface/contract assemblies) and `Framework Core` (implementations). This is a documented structural-role assignment, lower-confidence than the manifest Categories.
construction.other: src/OrchardCore.Themes/* -> Themes; src/Templates/* -> Templates; src/OrchardCore.Cms.Web + src/OrchardCore.Mvc.Web -> Hosting (the runnable web hosts).
construction.excluded: test/* projects, src/docs, and OrchardCore.Docs are not production architecture (matches the curation overlay's exclusions).

format: RSF `contain <cluster> <csproj-id>` tuples; entity ids are the `csharp:csproj:<repo-rel-path>` ids the pipeline's target-granularity graph export emits (so reference and recovered clusterings share an entity space).
rater_agreement: Single-transcriber, mechanical (regex over Manifest.cs). The eval §5.3 GT-doc protocol calls for two independent transcribers + reported kappa; because the module->Category mapping is a deterministic extraction from source (not a judgement call), a second human transcription is deferred. The judgement-laden part — the framework abstractions/core split and the theme/template/host roles — is flagged above as lower-confidence and is a stated threat.
caveats: Fragmentation: 28 module categories include ~17 singletons (Api, Tasks, Settings, GitHub, Google, X (Twitter), OpenID Connect, ...). OrchardCore's documented taxonomy is genuinely fine-grained; the reference reflects that and is not consolidated. A directory/dependency-based recovery will not recover singleton categories, which is an honest granularity-mismatch finding rather than a tool error.
The framework (101 of 207 projects, 49%) collapses into 2 clusters, so framework placement dominates MoJoFM. Report a2a and per-cluster c2c alongside.
C# is scored at TARGET (project) granularity only — the Roslyn helper emits no per-document references yet (open eval item), so OrchardCore has no file-granularity run.
